title: Edge Authorization Evidence Orchestration Playbook
author: Aisha Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the operational and compliance controls for collecting, packaging, and routing authorization and audit evidence from edge deployments (customer VPCs, on-premises gateways, and regional outposts). It explains RBAC constraints, minimal telemetry requirements, data residency considerations, secure SDLC hooks for evidence collection, incident response integration, and an exceptions workflow for proofs that cannot meet standard guarantees.

Audience: Security engineers, SREs supporting edge/private deployments, deployment leads, compliance officers, and support engineers involved in evidence collection and audit preparation.

Scope

- Applies to Redwood Private and dedicated edge connectors that run outside hosted control plane (VPC connectors, on-prem inference pods, and localized gateways).
- Covers authorization events, entitlement changes, service-to-service identity assertions, deployment rollouts that affect entitlements, and associated provenance metadata.
- Does NOT replace core enterprise audit pipeline; it augments the pipeline with edge-specific evidence packaging and proofchains.

Definitions

1) Authorization Evidence: the combined set of logs, policy snapshots, identity assertions, and manifests required to demonstrate who had what permission, when, and why.
2) Proof Bundle: signed, time-bounded archive of evidence prepared for audits or incident triage.
3) Edge Connector: software component deployed in a customer-managed environment to route inference requests and enforce tenancy controls.

Ownership and Roles

- Security (owner): policy definition, evidence schema, signing keys for Proof Bundles, and audit acceptance criteria.
- Edge Platform (owner): implement local collectors, ensure secure transport to Redwood evidence ingestion endpoints, and provide health/trust indicators.
- Customer Success: coordinate evidence handoffs with customers and legal for jurisdictional requests.

Policy Requirements (high-level)

- Minimum event set (must be captured at connector): authorization decisions (allow/deny), token issuance/rotation, role bindings, policy evaluation context (policy id + version), request context (route, model, tenant id), and deployment manifests (versioned).
- Cryptographic signing: Proof Bundles generated by the connector must be signed by a per-deployment key (customer-managed or Redwood-managed HSM). Signing metadata must reference the key rotation log.
- Immutability guarantees: local evidence must be append-only while retained locally; integrity proofs (merkle root or signatures) must be produced before local rotation or expiry.

Audit Logging and Retention

- Local retention baseline: 90 days of full fidelity logs within customer-managed storage for edge connectors.
- Central ingestion retention (Redwood): for ingested Proof Bundles, retain immutable copies for 7 years for enterprise customers requiring long-term retention, default retention 2 years for standard commercial customers.
- Redaction rules: PII must be redacted before central ingestion unless the customer contract and legal approvals permit transfer. A named redaction mapping must be included in the Proof Bundle manifest.

Secure SDLC Integration

- Build-time instrumentation: connectors must include a non-optional compile-time flag to enable evidence hooks. CI pipelines must run static analysis to ensure no evidence paths are disabled.
- Release gating: new connector releases require a policy-evidence conformance test in the release pipeline. Conformance artifacts (test vectors + results) are archived and referenced in the Proof Bundle when deployed.

Evidence Packaging: Proof Bundle Format (text table)

| Field | Description | Required |
| ----- | ----------- | -------- |
| bundle_id | UUID v4 | yes |
| signed_manifest.json | JSON manifest with schema_version, retention_policy, provenance | yes |
| auth_decisions.log | newline-delimited JSON, RFC 3339 timestamps | yes |
| policy_snapshot.tar.gz | tarball of active policy/role files (versioned) | yes |
| key_rotation.log | chronological list of key ids and thumbprints | conditional |
| redaction_map.json | keys that were removed/redacted | conditional |
| provenance.sig | detached signature over signed_manifest.json | yes |

Operational Playbook — Normal evidence collection

1) On connector start: generate ephemeral evidence-session-id and include in all auth decision logs.
2) Continuous: write auth_decisions.log locally; once per 6h generate signed_manifest.json and append provenance.sig.
3) Weekly: rotate local digest anchor (Merkle root) and push incremental Proof Bundle to Redwood ingestion endpoint over TLS 1.3 with mutual auth.
4) On deployment/role-change: produce on-demand Proof Bundle that includes the pre-change and post-change policy_snapshot. Mark this bundle asPriority=high.

Operational Playbook — Incident-triggered evidence flow

1) Triage kickoff: incident commander decides whether edge evidence should be exported immediately.
2) If yes: run the emergency evidence workflow (CLI or API) that instructs connector to compile a time-bounded Proof Bundle covering T0-6h to T0+6h.
3) Connector generates Proof Bundle, signs with the current key, and streams to a quarantined Redwood evidence ingestion endpoint.
4) Security team verifies bundle signature and performs integrity checks (signature validation, manifest schema).
4a) If signature verification fails: escalate to oncall (security) and preserve local artifacts per legal hold.

Exception and Approval Process

- Exception reasons: no outbound connectivity, local storage constraints, legal prohibition on cross-border transfer, or HSM unavailability.
- Approval flow: deployment owner opens an exception request ticket with an evidence fallback plan. Security and Compliance must jointly approve and attach compensating controls (e.g., on-demand remote joint-collection sessions with customer-located auditors, air-gapped USB-copy manifests held by legal).

Compensating Controls (examples)

- Where cross-border transfer is prohibited: retain full-fidelity logs in local jurisdiction and provide time-stamped digest + witness-signed manifest to Redwood.
- Where outbound connectivity is absent: enable offline Proof Bundle export (signed, physically transferred) with chain-of-custody checklist.

Operational Requirements and SLOs

- Evidence ingestion success: 99.9% of scheduled Proof Bundles must arrive at central ingestion within 24 hours under normal connectivity.
- Emergency export: connectors must be capable of generating an emergency Proof Bundle in <= 10 minutes.

Telemetry and Monitoring

- Health signals: last_successful_bundle_ts, last_signature_validation_ok, pending_bundle_size_bytes, error_rate_push_attempts.
- Alerts: page SRE on evidence_ingest_failure > 3 consecutive attempts or pending_bundle_size_bytes > 500MB for > 12h.

Integration with Incident Response

- Evidence preservation is a top-level priority in incidents affecting authorization. Incident commander should reference this playbook in the first 15 minutes of triage if authorization, entitlements, or access anomalies are suspected.
- For legal hold: compliance will issue a preservation order which freezes local deletion and marks bundles with hold=true. Connectors must honor hold flag and surface evidence export-only mode.

Compliance Acceptance Criteria

- A Proof Bundle is considered audit-ready when: signature verification succeeds, manifest schema_version is current (v2.1 as of this doc), redaction_map present if PII removed, and policy_snapshot includes a checksum that matches the deployment manifest.

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets

# generate on-demand bundle
redwood-edgectl evidence create --window "2026-06-01T08:00Z/2026-06-01T20:00Z" --priority high --output /var/tmp/pb-20260601.tar

# push bundle to central ingress (mutual TLS)
redwood-edgectl evidence push --file /var/tmp/pb-20260601.tar --endpoint ingress-evidence.redwood.internal --cert /etc/redwood/edge-cert.pem

Appendix B — Quick checklist for auditors

- Verify bundle_id is present and unique.
- Confirm provenance.sig verifies against known key thumbprint.
- Ensure policy_snapshot contains matching deployment hashes referenced in release pipeline artifacts.
- Check redaction_map for PII removal and legal basis for transfer.

References and Related Policies

- Authorization logging and deprovisioning guidance (rbac-and-auth).
- Audit schema and evidence tagging standard (audit-logging).
- Geo-smart retention policy and cross-border evidence playbook (data-residency-and-retention).
